questions.question: What does it mean that $f\colon A\to\mathbb R^m$ is locally injective at an interior point $x_0$ of $A$, with $b_0=f(x_0)$?
options: Each value $b$ near $b_0$ is attained by some $x$ near $x_0$
No nearby equation $f(x)=b$ has two nearby solutions
$f$ is injective on the whole of its domain $A$
The equation $f(x)=b_0$ is solved by the point $x_0$ itself

questions.question: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let $f\colon A\to\mathbb R^m$, and let $x_0\in\operatorname{int}(A)$ with $b_0=f(x_0)$. When is $f$ locally bijective at $x_0$?
options: When it is locally injective or locally surjective at $x_0$
When $f$ is a bijection from its whole domain onto $\mathbb R^m$
When $f(x)=f(x_0)$ has exactly one solution in the domain
When each $b$ near $b_0$ has exactly one solution near $x_0$

questions.question: Why do the definitions require $x_0$ to be an interior point of the domain $A$?
options: So that a whole ball around $x_0$ lies in $A$
So that $f(x_0)$ is an interior point of the image
So that $f$ is continuous at the point $x_0$
So that $f$ is differentiable at the point $x_0$

questions.question: Can a function be locally injective at every point of its domain without being injective?
options: No: local injectivity everywhere adds up to injectivity
No, at least not for continuous functions
Yes: $t\mapsto(\cos t,\sin t)$ repeats with period $2\pi$
Only if its domain is not a connected set

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be $C^1$ with $Df(x_0)=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$. What do the Jacobian rank criteria establish at $x_0$?
options: Local surjectivity only, from the nonzero first row
No local property is guaranteed by the criteria
Local injectivity only, since a column is nonzero
Local bijectivity, as the matrix is square

questions.question: Let $f(x)=x$ for $x\le0$ and $f(x)=x+1$ for $x>0$. Which local properties hold at $x_0=0$?
options: Locally bijective, since $f$ is strictly increasing
Locally surjective, since $f$ is increasing
Neither, since $f$ is not continuous at $0$
Locally injective, but not locally surjective

questions.question: For $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $f(x)=x^2$, use the input neighbourhood $U=(0.5,1.5)$ of $x_0=1$ and the output neighbourhood $V=(0.25,2.25)$ of $f(1)=1$. Which solution of $f(x)=1.21$ lies in $U$?
options: $x=1.1$, the solution near $x_0$
$x=-1.1$, the negative square root
Both $x=1.1$ and $x=-1.1$ count
None, since $1.21\ne f(x_0)$

questions.question: For the projection $f(x,y)=x$ near a point $(x_0,y_0)$, how many nearby solutions does $f(x,y)=b$ have when $b$ is close to $x_0$?
options: Exactly one, namely the point $(b,y_0)$
None at all, because $f$ ignores $y$
Infinitely many, one for each nearby $y$
At most one, because $f$ is a linear map

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be $f(x,y)=(x,y,x+y)$, and let $0<\varepsilon<0.01$. Which target near $f(0,0)=(0,0,0)$ has no solution?
options: $b=(\varepsilon,0,\varepsilon)$
$b=(0,0,\varepsilon)$
$b=(\varepsilon,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon)$
$b=(0,\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$

questions.question: For $f(x)=x^3$ at $x_0=0$, where $f'(0)=0$, which local properties hold?
options: Neither of them, since $f'(0)=0$
Uniqueness of nearby solutions only
Every nearby $b$ is attained, but not uniquely
Local bijectivity, despite $f'(0)=0$

questions.question: Let $a\in\mathbb R$ and let $f\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be $C^1$ with $Df(x_0)=\begin{pmatrix}a&1\\2&a\end{pmatrix}$. For which values of $a$ does the determinant criterion guarantee local bijectivity at $x_0$?
options: $a\ne0$
$a\ne2$

questions.question: For a $C^1$ map $f\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ with $n<m$, which local property can the rank criteria establish?
options: Local surjectivity, through full row rank
Local bijectivity, through a nonzero determinant
Local injectivity, through full column rank
None of them, since $n\ne m$

questions.question: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $f\colon A\to\mathbb R^m$, and $x_0\in\operatorname{int}(A)$. Define $g(x)=cf(x)+d$, where $c\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and $d\in\mathbb R^m$. How do the local properties of $g$ at $x_0$ compare with those of $f$?
options: All three properties are preserved only when $c>0$
Only local injectivity is necessarily preserved
Only local surjectivity is necessarily preserved
All three local properties are preserved.

questions.question: For $f(x,y)=(x,y^2)$ near $x_0=(1,0)$, how many nearby solutions does $f(x,y)=(1,\varepsilon)$ have for small $\varepsilon>0$, and for small $\varepsilon<0$?
options: One for $\varepsilon>0$ and one for $\varepsilon<0$
Two for $\varepsilon>0$, none for $\varepsilon<0$
Two in both cases, $(1,\pm\sqrt{|\varepsilon|})$
None for $\varepsilon>0$, two for $\varepsilon<0$

questions.question: For $f(x)=x^2$ at $x_0=2$, which interval is a neighbourhood of $x_0$ on which $f$ is injective?
options: No interval, since $x^2$ is not injective

questions.question: For $f\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$, $f(x,y)=x^2+y$, which nearby point solves $f(x,y)=-\varepsilon$ when $0<\varepsilon<0.01$?
options: $(\sqrt\varepsilon,0)$
None, since $x^2\ge0$
$(0,-\varepsilon)$
$(\varepsilon,-\varepsilon)$

questions.question: If $f$ is $C^1$ and locally injective at $x_0$, must $Df(x_0)$ have full column rank?
options: Yes, by the rank criterion of the theorem
Yes, since injectivity passes to the derivative
No, but $Df(x_0)$ must then have full row rank
No: $t\mapsto(t^3,t^3)$ is injective, yet $Df(0)=0$

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $f(x)=x^4-x^2$, and let $x_0=0$ with $b_0=f(0)=0$. How does the position of $b_0$ in the global image relate to local surjectivity at $x_0$?
options: $b_0$ is a boundary point of the image, and local surjectivity fails
$b_0$ is an interior point of the image, but local surjectivity fails
$b_0$ is an interior point of the image, and local surjectivity holds
$b_0$ is a boundary point of the image, but local surjectivity holds

questions.question: Let $f\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be $f(x,y)=(x,-x^2-y^2)$. Its Jacobian at $(0,0)$ has rank $1$. Which local properties actually hold at $(0,0)$?
options: Neither local injectivity nor local surjectivity
Local injectivity only, since the first output fixes $x$
Local surjectivity only, as the rank is $1$
Both, since the map is smooth

questions.question: Writing $z=x+\mathrm{i}y$, the map $z\mapsto z^3$ is $f(x,y)=(x^3-3xy^2,\ 3x^2y-y^3)$. For small $w\ne0$, how many solutions of $z^3=w$ lie near the origin?
options: Exactly one, as for the real cube $x^3$
None, since $Df(0,0)$ is the zero matrix
Three, all at distance $|w|^{1/3}$ from $0$
One when $w$ is real, otherwise none
